title: Amazon Order Scraper — Library Research & Decision
description: Notepad recording the evaluation of open-source Amazon order/transaction scrapers and the library chosen to anchor the Merchant-Transaction-Details project.
goal: Pick the most active, well-used open-source project to download Amazon order and transaction details (amounts, dates, summaries, full details) from a user's account using their credentials + MFA.
requirements: Support MFA / OTP / two-step verification prompts
Retrieve transaction amounts and transaction dates
Retrieve a nicely formatted summary and full order details
Usable as an embeddable library (not just a browser extension)
Actively maintained and reasonably widely used
Permissive open-source license suitable for redistribution

candidates.name: amazon-orders
candidates.author: alexdlaird
candidates.activity: very active (CI-tested, frequent releases, current as of research date)
notes: Parses Amazon's English (.com) consumer site; other locales not officially supported.
MFA via interactive OTP prompt or automated TOTP using AMAZON_OTP_SECRET_KEY env var.
full_details=True fetches per-order line items at the cost of one extra request per order.

candidates.name: azad
candidates.author: philipmulcahy
candidates.supportsMfaOtp: N/A (uses the user's already-logged-in browser session)
candidates.rejectionReason: Browser extension, not an embeddable library for an installable PC app; can't be driven headlessly from our own UI.

candidates.name: Amazon-Order-History
candidates.author: MaX-Lo
candidates.rejectionReason: Targets amazon.de only; lower activity; no robust MFA handling.

candidates.name: amzscraper
candidates.author: tobiasmcnulty
candidates.rejectionReason: Selenium-based, generates receipt PDFs; no structured transaction model, brittle, heavier dependency footprint.

candidates.name: amazon_order_history_scraper
candidates.author: drewdaemon
candidates.rejectionReason: Basic CSV export; no transactions API, no MFA, not maintained as a library.

candidates.name: LLM-Scraper
candidates.author: safffrron
candidates.rejectionReason: Relies on an LLM + Selenium to interpret pages; expensive, slow, and brittle for a packaged consumer app.

rationale: Most actively maintained candidate with a release dated the day of this research.
First-class, structured support for both orders (with line items / full details) and transactions (amounts + dates) — exactly the data we need.
Native MFA/OTP support (interactive prompt and automated TOTP secret), which is a hard requirement.
Clean Python library API plus a CLI, so it embeds directly into our installable PC app and headless flows.
MIT license permits redistribution inside our application.
Pure-HTTP parsing (no Selenium/browser) keeps the install small and easy to package for a PC.
risks: Unofficial scraper — may break when Amazon changes site structure; mitigate by pinning a version and tracking upstream releases.
Officially supports only the English amazon.com locale.
Amazon WAF/captcha challenges may require user interaction on some logins.

phase1: Record library research + decision in this JSON notepad
Scaffold an installable Python app with a simple UI (credentials, MFA, endpoint config)
Integrate amazon-orders to download orders + transactions and export a formatted JSON file
phase2_deferred: Optional HTTP PUT of the exported transaction JSON to a user-configured web endpoint
